column2: RETRACTION — the 2015-19 baseline is a contaminated PEAK, not a norm (Will challenge)
column4: Student 90+ share roughly DOUBLED then plateaued: 6.19% (2003) -> 11.40% (2015). Against 2003-07 (6.66%) today's 10.60% is +3.94pp; against 2008-11 (8.42%) +2.18pp; against 2015-19 (11.12%) -0.52pp. Same number, three baselines, opposite conclusions.
column7: Will asked whether the comparison years were themselves elevated. THEY WERE. DOCUMENTED CAUSE: for-profit college enrollment peaked 2010 at ~2.4M (~11% of all students) and fell ~50% by 2020; for-profits enrolled ~10% of students but accounted for ~50% of all defaults (~14.7% three-year default rate); those cohorts entered repayment 2012-2016 - exactly the climb-and-plateau window. Corinthian collapsed 2015, ITT 2016. The 2012-19 level therefore embeds a high-risk cohort that no longer exists at that size, making it the WRONG counterfactual for a 2026 portfolio. WHAT SURVIVES BEST: the FLOW comparison, because flow carries no accumulated stock - 7.83% today vs 10.10% (2012-14), 9.51% (2015-19), 8.11% (2008-11), 6.94% (2004-07) => back to roughly 2008-2011 levels, though ABOVE 2004-07, so 'below the entire pre-pandemic range' was also cherry-picked. Pre-pandemic flow was ALREADY DECLINING (2012-19 trend -0.037pp/qtr), consistent with the for-profit cohort washing out, which makes today's low flow less surprising rather than more. CONSEQUENCE: STUE's own 1RED->ORANGE dashboard downgrade was WITHDRAWN the same session - a downgrade needs positive evidence and that evidence is contested. NET: no clean baseline exists (2012-19 contaminated by for-profits; 2003-07 a far smaller and less-indebted book; all pre-2020 windows by IDR/PSLF/Fresh Start changing whether a struggling borrower even APPEARS delinquent). METHOD LESSON: the morning's finding came from asking 'compared to what?'; the correction came from asking it one level deeper - 'and was THAT period normal?' - and the stopping point happened to be the window that made the result strongest.

column7: PRIMARY: FSA PortfoliobyLoanStatus.xls + DLPortfoliobyDelinquencyStatus.xls (FedManagedPortbyDelinquencyStat tab), pulled 2026-08-13. RESOLVES open question #17 and REVERSES the morning's headline reading. The registered prior (composition-adjusted baseline sits BELOW 11.12%, making today's 10.60% ELEVATED) is CONFIRMED - but by a mechanism NOT anticipated: the dominant effect is denominator padding by the forbearance block, not for-profit cohort quality. WHY IT IS CONSERVATIVE: the in-repayment base EXCLUDES the defaulted stock, which grew 5.2M->9.0M in the two quarters immediately before this reading, so the WORST loans were removed from the denominator right before it was measured - a cleaner base should print LOWER and it printed higher. CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY PRIOR COMPARISON: the NY Fed headline rate is NOT comparable across the pandemic without an exposure adjustment; every 'back to pre-pandemic' claim (WALTER's May signal, CARL's framing, STUE's own morning finding) is a ratio whose denominator moved underneath it. STILL NOT DONE: (a) the for-profit cohort adjustment, which would push the pre-pandemic baseline lower still and make today look worse - unmeasured, so not claimed; (b) selection into forbearance is NOT controlled and could cut either way - the 2024-26 block is largely SAVE LITIGATION forbearance (administrative, not distress-selected), so the residual in-repayment population is not obviously adversely selected, but it may be POSITIVELY selected. (b) is the main threat to this finding -> open question #18.
